words.meaning: Something that is hard to do or understand.
To form a picture in your mind.
Words or images made by a machine on paper.
Physical objects or material.

medium.simple_explanation: In this context, it refers to written or printed materials and physical items.
medium.funny_explanation: It's the stuff that actually matters—literally! It’s all the physical papers and books that take up space in your bag.

examples.text: The library was full of printed matter like magazines and books.
My backpack is stuffed with so much printed matter that I might tilt backward.

words.meaning: Signs or facts that prove something is true.

medium.simple_explanation: Signs or facts that prove something exists or is true.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the chocolate smudge on your cheek that proves you're the one who ate the last brownie.

examples.text: Scientists look for evidence before they believe a new theory.
The pile of wet towels is evidence that the dog didn't enjoy his bath.

words.meaning: Magazines about a specific subject or hobby.

medium.simple_explanation: Regularly published magazines or newspapers, often about specific topics.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a blog, but on paper and usually written by people with fancy degrees.

examples.text: Doctors read medical journals to stay updated on new cures.
I tried to start a journal about my cat, but it was just 50 pages of 'he slept again'.

words.meaning: Pictures made using paint.

medium.simple_explanation: Pictures created by applying paint to a surface.
medium.funny_explanation: What happens when you combine a brush, some colors, and a lot of 'I hope this looks like a tree'.

examples.text: The museum displayed famous oil paintings from the 1800s.
My finger paintings were masterpieces until my mom mistook them for a spilled smoothie.

words.meaning: A place where plays and shows are performed.

medium.simple_explanation: A place where plays, movies, or shows are performed for an audience.
medium.funny_explanation: A room where you pay to watch people pretend to be other people while you try not to crunch your popcorn too loudly.

examples.text: We bought tickets to see a play at the local theatre.
I’m so dramatic that my kitchen becomes a theatre every time I drop a spoon.

words.meaning: Relating to a position of authority.

medium.simple_explanation: Something that is formal, authorized, or comes from a person in power.
medium.funny_explanation: The difference between 'my friend said so' and 'the principal wrote it on fancy paper'.

examples.text: The government issued an official statement about the new rules.
It’s not an official snow day until the news says I can go back to sleep.

words.meaning: Printed notices sent to many people at once.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author lists this to show that print is not just in books, but also in everyday official notices meant for many people.
hard.simple_explanation: Official letters or notices that are sent to many people at once.
hard.funny_explanation: It is like a group chat message, but on paper, and usually much more boring because it is from an official office.

examples.text: The school sent out circulars to inform parents about the upcoming holidays.
If I sent circulars to all my friends, they would probably think I was running for President of the Playground.

hard.real_world_analogy: A circular is like a mass email sent to everyone in a company; it is meant to go 'around' to everyone.

words.meaning: Charts showing the days and months of the year.
Books for writing down daily personal thoughts.
Notices used to help sell products or services.

medium.simple_explanation: Notices or short films used to persuade people to buy things.
medium.funny_explanation: Those annoying interruptions that tell you to buy a burger while you're trying to watch a cat video.

examples.text: The newspaper was full of colorful advertisements for new cars.
I saw so many advertisements for gym clothes that I felt tired just looking at them.

words.meaning: Large printed pictures used for decoration or news.
Books and writings that are considered artistic.

medium.simple_explanation: Written works like books, poems, and plays that are considered important art.
medium.funny_explanation: A very fancy way of saying 'books that your teacher thinks are really, really cool'.

examples.text: She spent the afternoon reading classic English literature.
Technically, the back of the cereal box is the first literature I read every day.

words.meaning: Pictures or statues of people or things.
To follow the progress or movement of something.
Related to all the people in a community.
Formal discussions where people express different opinions.

medium.simple_explanation: Formal discussions where people share different opinions on a topic.
medium.funny_explanation: An argument where you have to be polite and wait for your turn to talk, even if you’re 100% sure the other person is wrong.

examples.text: The students held a debate about whether they should have less homework.
My brothers have daily debates about who is actually the favorite child.

words.meaning: To come into sight or become visible.
To accept something as true without thinking.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe how we assume print will always be there without thinking about its history.
hard.simple_explanation: To accept something as true or always available without questioning it.
hard.funny_explanation: Assuming your socks will always be in the drawer without realizing your parents actually do the laundry.

examples.text: We take the internet for granted and forget how people lived without it.
My cat takes her daily treats for granted, acting like the world is ending if they are five minutes late.

hard.real_world_analogy: Taking oxygen for granted; you don't think about it until you try to hold your breath underwater.

words.meaning: To stop remembering something.
To suddenly understand or become aware.
The study of things that happened in the past.

medium.simple_explanation: The study of things that happened in the past.
medium.funny_explanation: A giant collection of stories about people who lived before smartphones existed.

examples.text: Learning about history helps us understand how the world works today.
My internet history is basically a record of all the weird questions I ask at 2 AM.

words.meaning: Influenced how something developed or became.

medium.simple_explanation: Influenced or formed the way something developed.
medium.funny_explanation: Like how a waffle iron turns a blob of batter into a delicious grid-patterned snack.

examples.text: Hard work and practice shaped her into a great athlete.
My obsession with pizza has shaped my personality (and my belt size).

words.meaning: Belonging to or occurring in the present time.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses it to explain how print has shaped the modern world we live in right now.
hard.simple_explanation: Belonging to or occurring in the present time.
hard.funny_explanation: Anything that is 'now-ish.' Using a smartphone is contemporary; using a carrier pigeon is definitely not.

examples.text: Contemporary artists use digital tools that didn't exist fifty years ago.
My grandma says my contemporary music sounds like a vacuum cleaner having a tantrum.

hard.real_world_analogy: A contemporary movie is one showing in theaters right now, compared to a black-and-white film from the 1920s.

words.meaning: To move around and reach many people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain how printed materials moved from one person or place to another.
hard.simple_explanation: To move around or pass from place to place or person to person.
hard.funny_explanation: The way a juicy piece of gossip travels through the school hallway at lightning speed.

examples.text: Newspapers began to circulate more widely as printing became cheaper.
I tried to circulate a petition to have pizza for every lunch, but the principal didn't sign it.

hard.real_world_analogy: Blood circulating through your body to reach every part, just like news reaching every person.

words.meaning: Relating to the present or recent times.
The process of growth or building something new.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Referring to the process of how printing technology grew and improved over time.
hard.simple_explanation: The process of starting to experience or create something new and better.
hard.funny_explanation: The long journey from a tiny seed to a giant plant, or from a baby's babble to a full-blown argument about chores.

examples.text: The development of the steam engine changed how people traveled.
The development of my gaming skills has reached 'pro' level, according to my mirror.

hard.real_world_analogy: The development of a butterfly from a caterpillar; it's a series of steps to become something more complex.

words.meaning: The first part or start of something.
A large region in the eastern part of Asia.

medium.simple_explanation: A region in the eastern part of Asia, including countries like China and Japan.
medium.funny_explanation: The place that gave the world the coolest inventions, from printing to some of your favorite cartoons.

examples.text: Printing technology first began to develop in East Asia.
I want to go to East Asia just to try every single type of ramen they have.

words.meaning: The act of becoming larger or spreading out.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe how printing technology spread from East Asia to Europe.
hard.simple_explanation: The action of becoming larger or more extensive.
hard.funny_explanation: What happens to your waistline after a very successful Thanksgiving dinner.

examples.text: The expansion of the Roman Empire took hundreds of years.
The expansion of my toy collection has officially taken over the entire living room floor.

hard.real_world_analogy: Blowing air into a balloon; as you blow, the surface expands and covers more space.

words.meaning: A continent located to the west of Asia.

medium.simple_explanation: A continent located to the west of Asia, known for its history and cultures.
medium.funny_explanation: A place where you can drive for two hours and end up in a different country with a different language and better bread.

examples.text: Print culture expanded rapidly throughout Europe in the 15th century.
In Europe, they call 'soccer' football, which makes sense because they actually use their feet.

words.meaning: A large country located in South Asia.

medium.simple_explanation: A large country in South Asia known for its diverse history and traditions.
medium.funny_explanation: The home of spicy food, colorful festivals, and 1.4 billion people who all love cricket.

examples.text: India has a rich history of hand-written manuscripts.
If you can survive the traffic in India, you can survive anything.

words.meaning: To know the meaning or purpose of something.
A powerful effect that something has on others.

medium.simple_explanation: A strong effect or influence that something has on a situation.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the 'impact' a cannonball splash has on everyone sitting by the pool.

examples.text: The invention of the smartphone had a huge impact on how we talk.
My joke had zero impact because nobody in the room understood the meme.

words.meaning: To cover a larger area or reach more people.
Scientific knowledge used to make tools.

medium.simple_explanation: Scientific knowledge used to create tools and machines that solve problems.
medium.funny_explanation: The magic that lets you talk to someone on the other side of the planet using a piece of glass in your pocket.

examples.text: New technology is making it easier to produce books quickly.
To my grandma, the microwave is 'alien technology' that she doesn't trust.

words.meaning: To think carefully about a particular subject.
Relating to society and how people live together.
Ideas, customs, and behaviors of a group.

medium.simple_explanation: The different ways of life, customs, and beliefs of various groups of people.
medium.funny_explanation: The reason why some people eat with chopsticks, some with forks, and some with their hands—and all of them are right!

examples.text: Traveling helps us understand and respect different cultures.
My family culture involves a long discussion about what to eat for dinner while we are eating lunch.

words.meaning: Made or became different from before.
Society where communication happens through printed materials.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This is the core subject of the chapter, focusing on how print changed the way people think and live.
hard.simple_explanation: The collection of habits, beliefs, and social changes resulting from the mass production of books and newspapers.
hard.funny_explanation: A world where everyone is obsessed with reading stuff rather than just listening to the village storyteller's tall tales.

examples.text: The rise of print culture allowed more people to share their political ideas.
Print culture is why we have magazines about cats wearing hats instead of just drawing them on cave walls.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like 'Internet Culture' today determines how we meme and talk; 'Print Culture' determined how people discussed news in the 1800s.

words.meaning: One of the main parts of a book.

medium.simple_explanation: One of the main sections into which a book is divided.
medium.funny_explanation: The checkpoint you have to reach in a book before you’re allowed to go to sleep.

examples.text: Please read Chapter Seven before the class tomorrow.
I skipped a chapter and now I have no idea why the main character is talking to a dragon.

words.meaning: A specific period of time in history.

medium.simple_explanation: A particular period of history with special characteristics.
medium.funny_explanation: A long stretch of time that usually ends when someone invents a much cooler way of doing things.

examples.text: We are currently living in the information age.
My parents grew up in the 'Age of Landline Phones,' which sounds ancient to me.

words.meaning: A famous Persian book written in the sixteenth century.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: An example of a famous manuscript produced by hand before the printing press arrived.
hard.simple_explanation: A 13th-century Persian book on ethics and philosophy, famously illustrated in royal workshops.
hard.funny_explanation: A very old, very fancy, hand-made book that was much harder to make than your school notebook.

examples.text: The Akhlaq-i-Nasiri is a great example of the artistic skill used in ancient manuscripts.
If I had to hand-write the Akhlaq-i-Nasiri, my hand would probably fall off by page three.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a limited-edition, hand-painted designer sneaker, but in book form and from hundreds of years ago.

words.meaning: Relating to a king, queen, or their family.
A room or building where things are manufactured.

medium.simple_explanation: A room or building where things are made or repaired, often by hand.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a messy garage where all the cool stuff is built, but with slightly more organization.

examples.text: The artist worked in his workshop to finish the sculpture.
My desk is a workshop for turning perfectly good paper into crumpled-up balls.

words.meaning: The number sixteen in a specific sequence.
A period of time lasting one hundred years.
Words spoken for someone else to write down.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes how books were created before printing; one person spoke while others wrote it down.
hard.simple_explanation: To say words aloud so that they can be written down by someone else.
hard.funny_explanation: Acting like a bossy king while someone else does the hard work of actually writing your thoughts.

examples.text: The king dictated the new laws to his royal scribes.
I dictated my Christmas list to my brother, but he just wrote 'chores' for every item.

hard.real_world_analogy: Using 'Speech-to-Text' on a phone; you talk, and the phone (the scribe) does the writing.

words.meaning: A book or text containing pictures and drawings.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Explains that old books were not just text but also contained hand-drawn pictures.
hard.simple_explanation: Providing a book or newspaper with pictures or diagrams.
hard.funny_explanation: Adding cool drawings to a story so you don't have to use your imagination for every single detail.

examples.text: The manuscript was beautifully illustrated with scenes of royal life.
My brother illustrated his math homework with doodles of fire-breathing dragons.

hard.real_world_analogy: A comic book is basically a highly illustrated story where the pictures are just as important as the words.

words.meaning: The act of drawing pictures to explain a text.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To emphasize the manual art form of drawing pictures for books before machines took over.
hard.simple_explanation: The act of creating pictures or drawings intended for publication in a book.
hard.funny_explanation: The professional version of doodling in the margins of your notebook, but people actually pay you for it.

examples.text: Illustrating a single book could take many months for a medieval artist.
I tried illustrating my life story, but it mostly looks like stick figures eating snacks.

hard.real_world_analogy: It's like being a director for a movie, but instead of cameras, you use pens and brushes to show the audience what is happening.

words.meaning: Having great value, meaning, or influence.
Different types or kinds of something.
Tools with moving parts that help do work.
Machines or tools used to do work.

medium.simple_explanation: The use of scientific knowledge and tools to make things or solve problems.
medium.funny_explanation: Basically any tool that isn't a plain old stick, though woodblocks were basically very fancy sticks.

examples.text: Hand-printing was the earliest kind of print technology used in China.
My phone is a piece of high-end technology, but I mainly use it to look at pictures of grumpy cats.

words.meaning: Created or made better over time.
A set way of doing something.
From a certain time or point forward.
Moving something against a surface.
Created for the first time.
The outer layer of something.
Wood pieces carved for printing.

medium.simple_explanation: Blocks of wood with carved designs or words used to stamp ink onto paper.
medium.funny_explanation: The ancient version of a 'copy-paste' button, made entirely out of trees.

examples.text: Books were printed by rubbing paper against the inked surface of woodblocks.
Don't get a splinter trying to print your essay with a woodblock!

words.meaning: Having tiny holes that let air through.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain why early Chinese 'accordion books' could only be printed on one side of the paper.
hard.simple_explanation: Having tiny holes or spaces that allow liquid or air to pass through.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a slice of Swiss cheese trying to hold water—that's porous! It's like a paper sieve that lets ink soak through to the other side.

examples.text: The porous paper absorbed the ink quickly, making double-sided printing impossible.
My porous raincoat was so full of holes that I was wetter inside than outside!

hard.real_world_analogy: A sponge is the ultimate porous object; it's practically made of tiny doorways for water.

words.meaning: Following old ways or customs.

medium.simple_explanation: A way of doing something that has been done the same way for a long time.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'Original Gangster' way of doing things before modern gadgets made everything boring.

examples.text: The traditional Chinese book was folded and stitched at the side.
Traditional school involves actual paper; modern school involves 47 open tabs on a browser.

words.meaning: Folded like the bellows of an instrument.

medium.simple_explanation: Something that folds and unfolds in a zigzag pattern.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the musical instrument, but it makes zero noise and is much better at being a book.

examples.text: The accordion book was popular because it could be folded easily.
I tried to play my accordion book, but the only sound it made was my teacher sighing.

words.meaning: Bent one part over another.
Sewn together with a needle.

medium.simple_explanation: Joined or fastened together using thread and a needle.
medium.funny_explanation: Giving a book a 'medical procedure' so its pages don't run away and get lost.

examples.text: The pages of the book were folded and then stitched at the side.
If your pants rip, they get stitched; if your book rips, it just cries.

words.meaning: In an excellent way.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the high level of talent possessed by the craftsmen who copied calligraphy.
hard.simple_explanation: In an excellent or magnificent way.
hard.funny_explanation: Doing something so well that even the toughest judge would give you an 11 out of 10.

examples.text: The ancient books were superbly crafted with detailed woodblock prints.
The cat superbly ignored me even when I waved a giant tuna sandwich in its face.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a master chef flipping a pancake perfectly into the air and catching it without looking.

words.meaning: Having the ability to do something well.
People who make things by hand.

medium.simple_explanation: People who are very skilled at making things by hand.
medium.funny_explanation: People who have Level 100 skills in real-life crafting and don't need a YouTube tutorial.

examples.text: Superbly skilled craftsmen could duplicate beautiful writing with woodblocks.
These craftsmen were so good they could probably draw a perfect circle while riding a unicycle.

words.meaning: To make an exact copy.

medium.simple_explanation: To make an exact copy of something.
medium.funny_explanation: The fancy, historical way of saying 'Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V.'

examples.text: Printing allowed people to duplicate many books quickly.
I wish I could duplicate myself so my clone could do my homework while I nap.

words.meaning: Unusual or surprising.

medium.simple_explanation: Very surprising or unusual in a way that deserves attention.
medium.funny_explanation: Something so cool that you actually want to talk about it instead of falling asleep.

examples.text: The woodblock prints showed remarkable accuracy in every detail.
It is remarkable how quickly a bag of chips disappears when I'm watching a movie.

words.meaning: Being correct and exact.

medium.simple_explanation: The quality of being correct, precise, or exact.
medium.funny_explanation: Like hitting the bullseye on a target instead of accidentally hitting your neighbor's window.

examples.text: The printers worked with great accuracy to copy the calligraphy.
My accuracy in throwing paper into the trash is 0%, but my accuracy in missing is 100%.

words.meaning: The art of beautiful handwriting.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text highlights this as the traditional art of beautiful writing that craftsmen aimed to duplicate.
hard.simple_explanation: The art of producing decorative and beautiful handwriting.
hard.funny_explanation: When your handwriting is so fancy and curvy that it looks like the letters are wearing tuxedos and dancing.

examples.text: The Diamond Sutra featured beautiful calligraphy alongside its illustrations.
I tried to do calligraphy, but my fancy 'A' looked like a spider had a very bad day on the page.

hard.real_world_analogy: If regular writing is like walking, calligraphy is like performing a professional ballet on paper.

words.meaning: Related to an empire or ruler.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the state of China under an emperor, which was the main producer of books.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to an empire, an emperor, or a supreme ruler.
hard.funny_explanation: Anything that has the 'King's Stamp' of approval and usually involves a lot of gold and fancy robes.

examples.text: The imperial state of China organized the printing of textbooks for civil service exams.
The toddler gave an imperial command for more cookies, pointing his juice box like a scepter.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like the 'Headquarters' of a massive global company, but for an entire country.

words.meaning: A country or its government.
Very important or large.
A person who makes something.
Things used to make something.
Had or owned something.

medium.simple_explanation: Owned, had, or controlled something.
medium.funny_explanation: Not the 'ghost in a haunted house' kind of possessed, just the 'I have this thing' kind.

examples.text: China possessed a huge system for hiring government workers.
He possessed five pizzas, but within ten minutes, they were gone.

words.meaning: Related to a complex government system.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain the large system of government officials in China that required many printed textbooks.
hard.simple_explanation: Related to a complex system of government with many rules and officials.
hard.funny_explanation: A giant maze of desks, forms, and 'please wait in line' signs where everyone has a specific stamp.

examples.text: China's bureaucratic system was so large that it needed millions of exam books.
To get a snack in this house, you have to follow a bureaucratic process of asking Mom, then Dad, then the Dog.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a school principal's office, but with a thousand principals and a million forms to fill out.

words.meaning: Found and hired for a job.

medium.simple_explanation: Persuaded or selected someone to join a group or do a job.
medium.funny_explanation: Like gathering a team for a heist, but with way more paperwork and fewer cool masks.

examples.text: The imperial state recruited its personnel through exams.
My mom recruited me for the 'Great House Cleaning Mission' last Saturday.

words.meaning: People who work for an organization.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the staff or people recruited into the Chinese civil service.
hard.simple_explanation: The people who work for an organization or government.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'humans' part of a machine; the people who actually do the work while wearing uniforms.

examples.text: The state recruited its personnel through difficult examinations.
The kitchen personnel (my brothers) were fired for eating all the cake before the party.

hard.real_world_analogy: The players on a football team are the personnel who make the game happen.

words.meaning: Related to ordinary citizens.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to ordinary citizens and their government, rather than military or religious matters.
medium.funny_explanation: Usually means 'being polite,' but in history class, it's just a fancy word for 'government stuff.'

examples.text: Students took civil service exams to get prestigious government jobs.
I try to be civil to my brother, but then he eats my last fry.

words.meaning: Formal tests of knowledge.
Very large in amount.
Support given by an organization.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes how the state paid for and supported the printing of textbooks.
hard.simple_explanation: Financial or official support provided by a person or organization.
hard.funny_explanation: When a big boss gives you the 'thumbs up' and a bag of money to get a job done.

examples.text: Under the sponsorship of the imperial state, textbooks were printed in vast numbers.
I am seeking sponsorship from the Tooth Fairy to fund my new video game habit.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a professional athlete wearing a logo because a company paid them to show it off.

words.meaning: People taking a test.

medium.simple_explanation: People who are applying for a job or taking an exam for a position.
medium.funny_explanation: A group of people who are currently sweating because they are being tested.

examples.text: The number of examination candidates increased significantly over time.
Candidates for the 'Best Snacker Award' include me, myself, and I.

words.meaning: Became larger in number.
Total amount of something.

medium.simple_explanation: The total amount or quantity of something.
medium.funny_explanation: Not how loud your music is, but how many things (like books) you are drowning in.

examples.text: The volume of print increased as more people took the exams.
The volume of laundry in my room is officially reaching mountain status.

words.meaning: Relating to a city.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to a city or town rather than the countryside.
medium.funny_explanation: Where there are more buildings than trees and more traffic than common sense.

examples.text: Urban culture bloomed in China as cities became centers of trade.
My urban lifestyle involves walking five steps to the nearest taco stand.

words.meaning: Developed in a successful way.
Changed to include many types.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To show how the uses of print expanded beyond just government exams to many other areas of life.
hard.simple_explanation: Increased the variety of things; branched out into many different areas.
hard.funny_explanation: Like a shop that only sold vanilla ice cream suddenly deciding to sell 50 flavors and hot dogs too.

examples.text: As urban culture bloomed, the uses of print diversified to include fiction and poetry.
My hobbies have diversified from just sleeping to also napping and snoring.

hard.real_world_analogy: A Swiss Army Knife is a diversified tool—it doesn't just cut; it opens cans, files nails, and pulls out splinters.

words.meaning: A person who studies deeply.

medium.simple_explanation: A person who is highly educated or has a lot of knowledge in a particular subject.
medium.funny_explanation: A professional nerd who actually gets respected for knowing a lot of stuff.

examples.text: Scholar-officials were the most educated people in the Chinese government.
I am a scholar of memes, with a PhD in internet jokes.

words.meaning: People in positions of authority.

medium.simple_explanation: People who hold a position of authority in an organization or government.
medium.funny_explanation: People who carry clipboards and look like they know exactly what's going on (even if they don't).

examples.text: The officials were responsible for running the civil service examinations.
The hall monitor is basically the most powerful official in our school.

words.meaning: People who buy and sell goods.

medium.simple_explanation: People who buy and sell goods in large quantities for profit.
medium.funny_explanation: The 17th-century version of Amazon sellers, minus the Prime shipping and drones.

examples.text: Merchants used print to keep track of their trade and business deals.
My cat is a merchant; he trades loud meows for midnight snacks.

words.meaning: Gathered together from places.
Buying and selling goods.
Facts about a subject.
More and more over time.
Time free from work.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe how reading became a fun activity for people's free time.
hard.simple_explanation: Time when one is free from work or duties; relaxation.
hard.funny_explanation: The glorious time when you can do absolutely nothing and not get in trouble for it.

examples.text: For the new urban readers, reading increasingly became a leisure activity.
My favorite leisure activity is staring at the ceiling and imagining I’m a billionaire.

hard.real_world_analogy: Leisure is like the weekend of your day—it's the 'me-time' after the 'work-time'.

words.meaning: Something that a person does.
Group of people who read.

medium.simple_explanation: The total group of people who read a particular book, newspaper, or magazine.
medium.funny_explanation: A 'ship' made entirely of people holding books instead of oars.

examples.text: The new readership in China included merchants and rich women.
The readership of my diary is strictly limited to me and my nosy sister.

words.meaning: Liked one thing more.
Stories that are not real.

medium.simple_explanation: Describing stories that are made up or imaginary, not based on real events.
medium.funny_explanation: Lies told so beautifully that you don't mind they aren't actually true.

examples.text: Readers in the cities loved fictional narratives about romance and adventure.
My excuse for why I didn't do my homework was purely fictional.

words.meaning: A story or description of events.

medium.simple_explanation: Stories or descriptions of a series of events.
medium.funny_explanation: A fancy-schmancy word for 'what happened next.'

examples.text: The new readership preferred exciting fictional narratives.
My life narrative is mostly just me looking for my lost socks.

words.meaning: Writing with rhythm and feelings.
Life stories written by the person.

medium.funny_explanation: Anything that makes your grandparents say, 'Back in my day, we didn't have this!'

examples.text: The printing press was the most advanced technology of its time.
My TV is high-end technology, but I still use it mostly for cat videos.

words.meaning: A machine used for printing books and newspapers.

medium.simple_explanation: A machine that applies pressure to ink and paper to create many copies of a text.
medium.funny_explanation: A giant heavy stamper that was basically the great-great-grandfather of your laser printer.

examples.text: The new press allowed people to print books much faster than writing by hand.
I tried to build a printing press out of textbooks and ink, but I just made a mess.

words.meaning: A hard material like iron, copper, or gold.
Small blocks used for printing letters on paper.

medium.simple_explanation: Small metal blocks with raised letters used to press ink onto paper.
medium.funny_explanation: Metal alphabet blocks for grown-ups who wanted to make books instead of towers.

examples.text: The printers used metal type to set the letters for each page of the Bible.
If I had a metal type for every time I forgot my homework, I'd have a whole library.

words.meaning: The decorative edges around a page or area.
Planned and made in a specific way or style.

medium.simple_explanation: Planned and made with a specific look or purpose in mind.
medium.funny_explanation: When you spend three hours choosing a font for a title that no one will notice.

examples.text: The borders of the pages were designed and painted by skilled artists.
I designed a perfect plan to sneak out for a snack, but I tripped over the dog.

words.meaning: Decorated by hand with bright colors and gold.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this to describe how early printed books were hand-decorated with bright colors or gold to make them look artistic.
hard.simple_explanation: Decorated with bright colors, gold, or silver by hand.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine taking your boring textbook and using 50 different glitter pens to make the borders look like a royal palace wall—that is illumination!

examples.text: The monk spent months creating an illuminated manuscript with gold leaf.
My notebook was so illuminated with neon highlighters that I needed sunglasses just to read my math notes.

hard.real_world_analogy: Adding fancy, colorful filters and stickers to a basic photo on Instagram to make it look special.

words.meaning: People who create art like paintings and drawings.
Almost the same but not exactly the same.
Checking two things to see how they differ.

medium.simple_explanation: Looking at two or more things to see how they are the same or different.
medium.funny_explanation: What your parents do when they look at your grades and then at your older sibling's grades.

examples.text: A careful comparison of the two books showed they were not identical.
A comparison between my cooking and my mom's proves that I should stick to cereal.

words.meaning: To show something that was not seen before.

medium.simple_explanation: To make something known or visible that was hidden before.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you move a pile of clothes and reveal the floor you haven't seen in weeks.

examples.text: Studying the books will reveal subtle differences in the hand-painted borders.
I’m waiting for the dramatic moment to reveal that I ate the last cookie.

words.meaning: The ways in which things are not alike.
A small group of powerful or rich people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It identifies the wealthy and powerful social group that preferred unique, hand-finished books over mass-produced ones.
hard.simple_explanation: A small group of powerful, wealthy, or high-ranking people.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'fancy-pants' crowd who only eat with silver spoons and think regular bread isn't 'exclusive' enough for them.

examples.text: In the 15th century, the elites were the only ones who could afford printed bibles.
The cat elites in our neighborhood only nap on silk cushions and refuse to chase common laser pointers.

hard.real_world_analogy: The VIP section at a concert where only the most famous or wealthy people get to sit.

words.meaning: In every place or in all directions.

medium.simple_explanation: In every place or all over.
medium.funny_explanation: Where dog hair ends up the second you buy a white couch.

examples.text: Rich people everywhere wanted these unique, hand-finished books.
I looked everywhere for my keys, only to find them in my hand.

words.meaning: Liked one thing more than another thing.

medium.simple_explanation: Liked one thing more than another.
medium.funny_explanation: I preferred the five-minute nap over the two-hour math lecture.

examples.text: The elites preferred books that were unique rather than mass-produced.
My cat preferred the cardboard box over the fifty-dollar bed I bought him.

words.meaning: Not having enough of something that is needed.
The state of being exactly the same throughout.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author explains that early books lacked uniformity because hand-painted details made every copy slightly different.
hard.simple_explanation: The quality of always being the same or consistent.
hard.funny_explanation: Like a colony of penguins where every single bird is wearing the exact same tuxedo and doing the exact same dance at the exact same time.

examples.text: The factory focused on uniformity to ensure every chocolate bar tasted exactly the same.
There was a total lack of uniformity in the dog parade; we had everything from a tiny chihuahua to a dog that looked like a small horse.

hard.real_world_analogy: A brand new pack of crayons where every 'Red' crayon is the exact same shade and length.

words.meaning: Had or owned something as a personal thing.

medium.simple_explanation: Owned or had something in one's possession.
medium.funny_explanation: Technically, I possessed a gym membership, but I only used it to buy smoothies.

examples.text: They possessed books that no one else in the world owned.
I possessed the secret password to the Wi-Fi, making me the king of the house.

words.meaning: Said that something belonged to them.

medium.simple_explanation: Stated that something belongs to you or is true.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you claimed you were 'just resting your eyes' but were actually snoring for an hour.

examples.text: Rich owners claimed their books were unique because of the hand-painted art.
He claimed he could do a backflip, but then he just fell over sideways.

words.meaning: Being the only one of its kind.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To emphasize that because of hand-painting, no two Gutenberg Bibles were exactly alike.
hard.simple_explanation: Being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.
hard.funny_explanation: Like a pizza topped with marshmallows and pickles—it might be weird, but there is definitely nothing else like it!

examples.text: Each copy of the book was unique because the borders were painted by different artists.
My brother has a unique talent for sneezing in the rhythm of the national anthem.

hard.real_world_analogy: A snowflake—even though there are billions, no two are ever shaped exactly the same.

words.meaning: To see or become aware of something.
Symbols used to write words and represent sounds.
Many different types of things or people.
The special purpose or the job of something.

medium.simple_explanation: The purposes or jobs that something is supposed to do.
medium.funny_explanation: The only functions of my alarm clock are to make me angry and to be hit repeatedly.

examples.text: The use of color in the letters had two important functions.
This app has many functions, but I only use the one that puts dog ears on my face.

words.meaning: Made a part of something stand out clearly.

medium.simple_explanation: Made something stand out so it attracts attention.
medium.funny_explanation: When you accidentally drop a bright yellow marker on your white shirt.

examples.text: The holy words were highlighted with bright colors to show their importance.
I highlighted the entire page of my textbook because everything seemed important.

words.meaning: Very special and connected to God or religion.
To show that something is very important.

medium.simple_explanation: To give special importance or attention to something.
medium.funny_explanation: How my teacher uses ten exclamation marks to emphasize that the essay is due tomorrow.

examples.text: Printers used color to emphasise the significance of certain words.
I tried to emphasize that I was hungry by staring sadly at the fridge.

words.meaning: The importance or meaning of something.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text explains that color was used on specific words to show how important or 'holy' they were.
hard.simple_explanation: The quality of being worthy of attention; importance.
hard.funny_explanation: The difference between your teacher saying 'Hello' and your teacher saying 'SURPRISE TEST'—the second one has much more significance!

examples.text: The color used in the text helped to emphasize the significance of holy names.
The cat did not understand the significance of the expensive vase; to him, it was just a fancy jumping obstacle.

hard.real_world_analogy: A giant red 'STOP' sign in a world of grey buildings; it stands out because it matters more.

words.meaning: Empty areas between words, letters, or objects.
A person who arranges text for printing.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To define the specific job of a person who arranged individual metal letters to form words for the printing press.
hard.simple_explanation: A person who arranges the metal type (letters) for printing.
hard.funny_explanation: A master of the world's most difficult 'Scrabble' game who has to pick up tiny metal letters and put them in a frame perfectly.

examples.text: The compositor worked quickly to arrange the metal letters before the ink dried.
I’m like a modern compositor when I spend twenty minutes trying to find the right emojis for one text message.

hard.real_world_analogy: A person building a giant wall out of LEGO bricks that each have a single letter printed on them.

words.meaning: To put different parts together to create something.

medium.simple_explanation: Puts together parts or elements to create a whole, like arranging letters for printing.
medium.funny_explanation: What a printer does with letters, and what I do with excuses for why I’m late.

examples.text: The compositor composes the text by picking out each individual metal letter.
She composes a grocery list but then leaves it on the kitchen counter.

words.meaning: A metal tray used to hold printing type.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To introduce the technical tool (a metal frame) used to hold the arranged type in place before printing.
hard.simple_explanation: A metal tray or frame that holds arranged type (letters) together.
hard.funny_explanation: A metal 'waiting room' where all the tiny letters sit in straight rows before they get pressed onto the paper.

examples.text: The printer carefully moved the galley of text to the press machine.
The letters in the galley looked like tiny soldiers standing in perfect formation, waiting for the ink battle.

hard.real_world_analogy: A baking tray that keeps all your cookies in neat, straight rows so they don't slide around.

words.meaning: A structure that holds or surrounds something.
Put or placed something down in a position.
A room where people make or fix things.
The number sixteen in a specific sequence.
A period of time lasting one hundred years.
Shows or represents something in a picture.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this word to explain what is being shown in the provided illustration of a workshop.
hard.simple_explanation: To show or represent something by a drawing or painting.
hard.funny_explanation: When you draw a circle with five sticks and tell people it 'depicts' your best friend at the beach.

examples.text: The 16th-century picture depicts the various stages of the printing process.
The cave painting depicts a hunter, but honestly, it looks more like a potato with legs.

hard.real_world_analogy: A map 'depicts' the real world but using lines and colors on a small piece of paper.

words.meaning: Things that are being done for a purpose.
The part of a picture closest to the viewer.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To help the reader locate specific workers (the compositors) in the front section of the historical diagram.
hard.simple_explanation: The part of a view or picture that is nearest to the observer.
hard.funny_explanation: The part of a group photo where your cousin makes a funny face so close to the camera that he's the only thing you see.

examples.text: In the foreground of the workshop, you can see the workers preparing the ink.
The mountains were in the background, but a giant squirrel was sitting in the foreground of my photo.

hard.real_world_analogy: The actors on a stage are in the foreground, while the painted trees behind them are in the background.

words.meaning: Made something ready for a task or use.
Put or spread something onto a surface.

medium.simple_explanation: Put or spread something onto a surface.
medium.funny_explanation: How you applied way too much hot sauce to your taco and now your mouth is a volcano.

examples.text: Ink is being applied on the metal types before they are pressed onto paper.
I applied sunscreen so thick that I look like a friendly ghost at the beach.

words.meaning: The part of a scene behind the main objects.

medium.simple_explanation: The part of a picture or scene that is behind the main objects.
medium.funny_explanation: Where you see your weird uncle doing a funny dance while you're trying to take a serious selfie.

examples.text: In the background of the workshop picture, you can see the printers working the press.
My Zoom background is a picture of a tropical beach, but I'm actually in a messy bedroom.

words.meaning: Metal pins used to hold things together tightly.
People who check printed text for any errors.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the workers whose job it was to check the printed sheets for any spelling or layout mistakes.
hard.simple_explanation: People who read a text to find and correct mistakes before it is published.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Grammar Police' who hunt down typos and missing commas like they are looking for hidden treasure.

examples.text: Proofreaders checked every page of the Bible to ensure there were no errors in the holy text.
If it weren't for proofreaders, your favorite book might be full of 'the' written as 'teh'.

hard.real_world_analogy: A coach who watches a video of your game to spot the tiny mistakes you made so you can fix them next time.

words.meaning: Coming at the very end of a process.
Large, flat, thin pieces of paper or material.
Put things neatly one on top of another.

medium.simple_explanation: Piled up neatly on top of each other.
medium.funny_explanation: How your dirty dishes look when you're trying to ignore them for a week.

examples.text: The printed sheets were stacked in neat piles waiting to be put together.
I stacked twenty pancakes on my plate, which was definitely a bad idea.

words.meaning: Organized and clean in a very good way.
Groups of things put on top of each other.
Fastened together to make a finished book.

medium.simple_explanation: Tied or fastened together, like the pages of a book attached to a cover.
medium.funny_explanation: Books are just a bunch of papers that are bound together so they don't run away.

examples.text: The printed sheets were waiting to be bound into a finished book.
I was bound to my chair by a very long movie and a very large bag of popcorn.

words.meaning: A big change in how things are done.

medium.simple_explanation: A giant change in the way something works or how people live.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when your room goes from a disaster zone to sparkling clean in 5 minutes because your parents are home—that’s a cleaning revolution.

examples.text: The print revolution changed how people shared information forever.
The invention of the air fryer was a dinner-time revolution for lazy cooks.

words.meaning: The process of growing or becoming better.
Completely changed the way something looks or works.

medium.simple_explanation: To change something completely, usually for the better.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a caterpillar turning into a butterfly, or me turning into a zombie after a 10-hour gaming session.

examples.text: The arrival of cheap books transformed the lives of ordinary people.
The messy garage was transformed into a cool hangout spot with just a few beanbags.

words.meaning: The way people or things are connected.
Facts or details about a subject.
Things you know from learning and experience.
Important groups like schools, banks, or churches.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe how print changed people's connection with large social systems like the Church or State.
hard.simple_explanation: Large, established organizations or systems that govern how society works.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of them as the 'Big Bosses' of society—like schools, the government, or the church—that usually have a lot of rules and big buildings.

examples.text: The printing press changed how people interacted with religious institutions.
Even the most serious institutions couldn't stop people from printing funny memes about them eventually!

hard.real_world_analogy: A school is an institution that organizes how you learn, just like a bank is an institution for money.

words.meaning: People who have the power to give orders.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text explains how the print revolution allowed people to question those in power.
hard.simple_explanation: People or groups who have the power to make decisions and enforce rules.
hard.funny_explanation: The people who get to say 'because I said so' and actually have the power to make you do it.

examples.text: The new ideas in books often challenged the ideas of the authorities.
The local authorities, also known as my parents, have banned ice cream before dinner.

hard.real_world_analogy: The referee in a football game is the authority who decides if you played by the rules.

words.meaning: Changed the way someone thinks or acts.

medium.simple_explanation: Having an effect on the way someone thinks, acts, or behaves.
medium.funny_explanation: My cat influenced my decision to stay in bed by sleeping on my legs and looking too cute to move.

examples.text: New printed books influenced how people looked at the world.
I was influenced by the pizza commercial to spend my entire allowance on extra cheese.

words.meaning: The way people understand or see things.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To show how printing changed the way people viewed and understood the world around them.
hard.simple_explanation: The way you notice, see, or understand something through your senses or mind.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like the 'filter' you use to look at the world; one person sees a rainstorm as sad, while another sees it as a free car wash.

examples.text: Print culture influenced popular perceptions of religion and science.
My perception of the 'giant monster' in the dark turned out to be just a pile of laundry.

hard.real_world_analogy: Wearing tinted sunglasses changes your perception of the color of the sky.

words.meaning: To study or look into something carefully.
To come out and become known.

medium.simple_explanation: To come out into the open or start appearing for the first time.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when a giant pimple emerges on your forehead right before school picture day.

examples.text: With the invention of the printing press, a new reading public emerged.
The sun finally emerged from the clouds, just as the picnic was officially cancelled.

words.meaning: Made something smaller in amount or price.
Hard work done using physical strength.

medium.simple_explanation: Hard physical or mental work.
medium.funny_explanation: The intense labour of trying to open a pickle jar when you are really, really hungry.

examples.text: Printing machines meant that less manual labour was needed to make books.
It took hours of labour to untangle the giant ball of holiday lights.

words.meaning: Something that is needed or necessary.
More than one or many.
Filled a place with too many things.

medium.simple_explanation: When a huge amount of something arrives or fills a space all at once.
medium.funny_explanation: Like how my phone gets flooded with 'where are u' texts when I'm five minutes late to meet my friends.

examples.text: Cheaply printed books soon flooded the markets in every town.
The kitchen was flooded with the smell of burnt popcorn.

words.meaning: The group of people who read a book.

medium.simple_explanation: The group of people who regularly read a particular book, magazine, or newspaper.
medium.funny_explanation: My personal diary has a readership of exactly one person—my annoying little brother who keeps stealing it.

examples.text: Publishers worked hard to grow their readership among common people.
The school newspaper's readership tripled when they started printing gossip about the teachers.

words.meaning: The chance or right to use something.
The habits and beliefs of a group.
Kept within certain limits or for few people.

medium.simple_explanation: Limited to a specific group of people or kept under strict control.
medium.funny_explanation: My access to the 'good snacks' is restricted by my mom’s secret hiding spot on the top shelf.

examples.text: Before printing, reading was restricted to the rich and powerful elites.
The VIP area at the concert was restricted to people who paid way too much money.

words.meaning: Rich and powerful people in a society.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To contrast the wealthy minority who could read before print with the common people who could not.
hard.simple_explanation: A small group of people who are considered superior because of their wealth, power, or talent.
hard.funny_explanation: The fancy-pants crowd who get the VIP seats and probably have gold-plated toothbrushes.

examples.text: Before the printing press, reading was a luxury restricted to the elites.
The cat elites only eat the finest tuna served on a silver saucer.

hard.real_world_analogy: The players on an All-Star team are the elites of their sports league.

words.meaning: Using spoken words instead of writing.

medium.simple_explanation: Related to the mouth or spoken words rather than written ones.
medium.funny_explanation: An oral tradition in my house is everyone shouting 'Not it!' when the dog poops on the rug.

examples.text: Before books were common, most people lived in a world of oral culture.
The teacher gave us an oral exam, so we had to speak our answers out loud.

words.meaning: Related to God or worthy of religious respect.

medium.simple_explanation: Something very holy, religious, or deserving of great respect.
medium.funny_explanation: The Wi-Fi password is considered sacred in this house; you don't just give it to anyone!

examples.text: Common people used to listen to sacred texts being read out in public.
In some cultures, cows are considered sacred and are treated very kindly.

words.meaning: The written words in a book or document.
Songs or poems that tell a popular story.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to explain how stories were traditionally shared through song and rhyme before everyone could read.
hard.simple_explanation: Simple songs or poems that tell a story, often about history or legends.
hard.funny_explanation: A musical story-time! Like a hit song on the radio, but instead of singing about a breakup, it's about a knight fighting a dragon.

examples.text: Printers began publishing popular ballads to attract people who liked listening to stories.
I wrote a ballad about the time I tripped over my own feet in the cafeteria.

hard.real_world_analogy: A ballad is like a movie trailer that you sing instead of watch.

words.meaning: Said a poem or story aloud from memory.

medium.simple_explanation: Said something out loud from memory in front of an audience.
medium.funny_explanation: I recited the entire fast-food menu to the waiter, only to realize I forgot to actually pick what I wanted to eat.

examples.text: Groups often gathered to hear ballads being recited by performers.
The toddler recited the alphabet, but skipped the letter Q because it looked too weird.

words.meaning: Told a story or described a series of events.

medium.simple_explanation: Told a story or described a series of events in detail.
medium.funny_explanation: I wish Morgan Freeman narrated my life every time I tripped over my own feet in the school hallway.

examples.text: The traveler narrated his adventures to the curious villagers.
The documentary was narrated by a guy who sounded like he was falling asleep.

words.meaning: Moved from one person or place to another.
By speaking rather than writing.

medium.simple_explanation: Done by speaking rather than writing.
medium.funny_explanation: I tried to do my math homework orally, but my teacher insisted on seeing the 'work' on paper. Rude.

examples.text: In the past, most knowledge was transferred orally from parents to children.
The secret code was shared orally so there would be no paper evidence.

words.meaning: Done by a group of people together.

medium.simple_explanation: Done by people acting together as a group.
medium.funny_explanation: My friends and I collectively decided that Monday should be banned forever.

examples.text: Villagers collectively gathered to hear the latest news from the printed broadsides.
The class collectively groaned when the teacher announced a pop quiz.

words.meaning: Acting, singing, or dancing for an audience.
Done by one person alone.
Doing something without making any sound.
Costing a large amount of money.
Having enough of what is needed.

medium.simple_explanation: Having enough of something for a particular purpose.
medium.funny_explanation: One slice of pizza is never sufficient; the laws of physics require at least three.

examples.text: Before the printing press, books were not available in sufficient numbers for everyone.
Is five minutes of studying sufficient for a final exam? Probably not.

words.meaning: Different parts or groups of something.
Process of changing from one thing to another.

medium.simple_explanation: The process of changing from one state or condition to another.
medium.funny_explanation: The transition from 'asleep' to 'awake' involves five alarms and a lot of regret.

examples.text: The transition from an oral culture to a reading culture took a long time.
The transition from winter to spring usually involves three weeks of sneezing.

words.meaning: A person who can read and write.

medium.simple_explanation: Being able to read and write.
medium.funny_explanation: I am very literate, except when I’m trying to read the instructions for building IKEA furniture.

examples.text: In the 16th century, very few people were literate enough to read a book.
My dog is so smart I almost expect him to become literate and write his own grocery list.

words.meaning: The ability to read and write.

medium.simple_explanation: The ability to read and write.
medium.funny_explanation: Emoji literacy is a real thing; I can tell exactly how mad my mom is by which smiley face she sends.

examples.text: Literacy rates were very low in Europe until the twentieth century.
High literacy means you can finally understand the plot of those confusing sci-fi movies.

words.meaning: A period of one hundred years.
People or companies that print and sell books.

medium.simple_explanation: People or companies that prepare and produce books or magazines for sale.
medium.funny_explanation: If I were a publisher, I’d only print books that come with free snacks and a nap schedule.

examples.text: Early publishers used pictures to attract people who couldn't read well.
The publishers were shocked when the book about 'How to Sleep' became a bestseller.

words.meaning: To make someone believe or do something.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain how publishers tried to convince common people to buy and enjoy books.
hard.simple_explanation: To convince someone to do or believe something through reasoning or argument.
hard.funny_explanation: Using your 'jedi mind tricks' to get your friend to trade their chocolate bar for your apple.

examples.text: Publishers had to persuade the public to welcome printed books.
I tried to persuade my dog that bath time is actually a spa day, but he didn't buy it.

hard.real_world_analogy: A lawyer's job is to persuade the jury that their client is innocent.

words.meaning: To accept something new with pleasure.
In very large or great amounts.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To emphasize that books for the common people were filled with many pictures.
hard.simple_explanation: In large amounts; abundantly.
hard.funny_explanation: Doing something way too much—like how a sweaty person drips after a 100-meter dash.

examples.text: The early printed books were profusely illustrated with pictures to attract readers.
He thanked his grandma profusely after she gave him twenty dollars for his birthday.

hard.real_world_analogy: When it rains in a rainforest, it rains profusely—there is water everywhere!

words.meaning: Decorated with pictures or drawings.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To show how visual elements made books accessible to those who couldn't read well.
hard.simple_explanation: Containing pictures, drawings, or diagrams to explain or decorate the text.
hard.funny_explanation: A book that isn't just a wall of boring gray words; it's got 'eye candy' to help you see the story.

examples.text: Folk tales were illustrated to make them more enjoyable for people who could not read.
I illustrated my science project with doodles of grumpy atoms.

hard.real_world_analogy: An illustrated book is like a movie with subtitles—the pictures tell the story even if you miss the words.

words.meaning: Meetings where many people come together.
Places where people drink, eat, and meet friends.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Identified as the social places where people gathered to hear news and stories.
hard.simple_explanation: Establishments where people gather to eat, drink, and socialize.
hard.funny_explanation: The old-school version of a neighborhood hang-out spot, minus the Wi-Fi and plus a lot of loud singing.

examples.text: Printed stories were often recited in village taverns for everyone to hear.
If I lived in the 1700s, I’d probably be in the tavern telling tall tales about catching a giant fish.

hard.real_world_analogy: Taverns were like the 'community centers' or 'coffee shops' of the past.

words.meaning: Passed on from one person to another.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe how information was passed from one person to another.
hard.simple_explanation: Passed on from one person, place, or thing to another.
hard.funny_explanation: Like passing a 'hot potato' of information from your mouth to someone else's ears.

examples.text: Before print, knowledge was transmitted orally through stories and performances.
The flu was transmitted through the classroom faster than a secret about a crush.

hard.real_world_analogy: A radio tower transmits signals to your car so you can hear music.

words.meaning: Kept apart or divided into parts.
Not clear or hard to see clearly.

medium.simple_explanation: When the edges of something become unclear or two different things mix together.
medium.funny_explanation: The line between 'just one more episode' and 'it's 4 AM' is very blurred when watching a good show.

examples.text: The line between hearing a book and reading a book became blurred.
Everything looked blurred until I realized I was wearing my grandma's glasses by mistake.

words.meaning: Mixed together with each other.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To show how the line between 'hearing' and 'reading' publics disappeared as they blended.
hard.simple_explanation: Mixed or blended together.

words.meaning: A building where Christians go to pray.
An alphabetical list of names or topics.

medium.simple_explanation: An alphabetical list of names, subjects, or items, often used for reference.
medium.funny_explanation: A giant 'To-Do' or 'Don't-Do' list that helps you find things without searching the whole building.

examples.text: The Index of Prohibited Books listed what people were not allowed to read.
I need an index for my backpack just to find my pencil at the bottom.

words.meaning: Not allowed or forbidden by a law.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It refers to the Index of Prohibited Books, which were texts the Church banned people from reading.
hard.simple_explanation: Something that is strictly forbidden or not allowed by law or authority.
hard.funny_explanation: Like the 'forbidden snacks' your mom hides on the top shelf—you know they exist, but you're definitely not supposed to touch them.

examples.text: The Church maintained a list of prohibited books to prevent the spread of ideas they disagreed with.
Running in the hallways is prohibited, but I think 'walking fast with style' should be allowed!

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a 'No Trespassing' sign on a fence that tells you exactly where you aren't allowed to go.

words.meaning: The middle part of the 1500s.
A famous leader who fought for India.
A word meaning self-rule for India.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It is used in the context of Gandhi’s fight for self-rule and freedom of the press in India.
hard.simple_explanation: Self-rule or independence, specifically referring to India's movement to govern itself.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like finally getting your own room and being the boss of the decor, the music, and when you go to bed, without anyone else’s rules.

examples.text: Gandhi believed that Swaraj was impossible without the liberty of speech and the press.
I declared Swaraj over my lunchbox today and refused to trade my cookies for carrot sticks.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a bird finally leaving the nest to build its own home and decide where it wants to fly.

words.meaning: The freedom to live as you wish.

medium.simple_explanation: The state of being free within society from oppressive restrictions.
medium.funny_explanation: The sweet, sweet feeling of doing what you want, like choosing your own topping on a pizza.

examples.text: Gandhi fought for the liberty of speech for all Indians.
I took the liberty of eating your fries because you looked like you were full.

words.meaning: The act of speaking to an audience.

medium.simple_explanation: The expression of or the ability to express thoughts and feelings by spoken words.
medium.funny_explanation: The sounds that come out of your mouth, ranging from 'I have a dream' to 'Can I have a cookie?'

examples.text: Freedom of speech is a fundamental right in many countries.
His speech was so boring that even the microphone fell asleep.

words.meaning: Newspapers, magazines, and the people writing them.

medium.simple_explanation: Newspapers, magazines, and the news media collectively.
medium.funny_explanation: The professional gossip-reporters who print the news and occasionally get chased by celebrities.

examples.text: Liberty of the press is essential for a healthy democracy.
The school press reported that the cafeteria food was 'questionable' at best.

words.meaning: The right to act and speak freely.

medium.simple_explanation: The power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without hindrance.
medium.funny_explanation: The magical ability to say 'no' to homework... until you realize the consequences.

examples.text: The fight for Swaraj was a fight for freedom of association.
Freedom is being able to sleep in on a Saturday without an alarm clock.

words.meaning: A group of people with the same aim.

medium.simple_explanation: A group of people organized for a joint purpose.
medium.funny_explanation: Basically a club, like the 'Cool Kids Club' or the 'People Who Wear Odd Socks' group.

examples.text: The freedom of association allows people to form political groups.
I belong to an association of people who believe breakfast should be served all day.

words.meaning: Not long in length or time.
Short written messages to help remember things.

medium.simple_explanation: A brief record of facts, topics, or thoughts, written down as an aid to memory.
medium.funny_explanation: The scribbles in your notebook that look like ancient hieroglyphics when you try to read them for the test.

examples.text: Write short notes about what you know concerning the Gutenberg Press.
My notes for math class are mostly just drawings of cool-looking swords.

words.meaning: To let someone look at something.
The man who invented the printing press.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Named after Johannes Gutenberg, the inventor of the first mechanical printing press which changed history.
hard.simple_explanation: The inventor who created the movable type printing press in the 15th century.
hard.funny_explanation: The original 'Tech Bro' of the 1400s; he didn't invent the internet, but he made books go viral before computers even existed.

examples.text: The Gutenberg Press allowed books to be produced much faster and cheaper than hand-copying.
If Gutenberg saw how fast my inkjet printer jams, he’d probably laugh at our modern technology.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like the difference between handwriting a 500-page novel by hand and just hitting 'Print' on a computer.

words.meaning: A famous scholar and writer from Europe.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Erasmus was a famous scholar who had mixed feelings about the explosion of printed books.
hard.simple_explanation: A Dutch philosopher and scholar known for his critical views on the Church and the quality of printed books.
hard.funny_explanation: The 16th-century version of a book critic who complained that there were too many 'bad' books being published and cluttering up the world.

examples.text: Erasmus was worried that the mass production of books would spread nonsense and errors.
I think Erasmus would have hated Twitter; imagine him complaining about all the 'useless' short messages!

hard.real_world_analogy: Like that one teacher who loves reading but gets annoyed when students only read comic books instead of the classics.

words.meaning: A thought or a suggestion.
Local language spoken by ordinary people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It refers to the Vernacular Press Act, which targeted newspapers written in local Indian languages.
hard.simple_explanation: The language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people of a particular country or region.
hard.funny_explanation: It's the 'home-speak' you use with your friends and family, rather than the super-fancy, formal language used in legal documents.

examples.text: The Vernacular Press Act was designed to control local language newspapers that criticized the British.
My 'vernacular' includes a lot of slang that my computer's spell-check definitely does not understand.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like the difference between texting 'Sup?' to a friend and writing 'Greetings, how do you do?' to a principal.

words.meaning: A law that has been passed.

medium.simple_explanation: A law or decree passed by a legislative body.
medium.funny_explanation: A very serious rule made by people in suits that everyone has to follow, even if they don't like it.

examples.text: The Vernacular Press Act restricted the freedom of Indian newspapers.
If I were king, my first act would be to make ice cream free on Tuesdays.

words.meaning: To have a particular sense or significance.
People who try to improve society.

medium.simple_explanation: People who work to improve a social, political, or economic system.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'fix-it' crew of history who see something wrong and try to make it right for everyone.

examples.text: Reformers in India used print to spread ideas about social change.
The reformers of the lunchroom successfully replaced mystery meat with tacos.
